headline: A multinational advisory unmasked Russia's Laundry Bear running a zero-click Zimbra webmail campaign that lifted mail and two-factor codes from Western governments, as ransomware crews squeezed a Swiss rail maker and Japan's frozen-food supply.

emerging_trends.text: State-backed espionage keeps flowing through everyday collaboration software, with Russia's Laundry Bear reading Western governments' mail through Zimbra and a China-nexus crew probing the same government, healthcare, and education sectors.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Laundry Bear Runs Zero-Click Zimbra Webmail Espionage

emerging_trends.text: Attackers increasingly launder their operations through trusted software, weaponizing GitHub Actions runners against hosting servers and disguising malware as a Notepad++ plugin so the activity blends into ordinary developer work.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Malware Rides GitHub Actions and Notepad++ Plugins

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware crews keep entering through suppliers, as Everest hit a Swiss rail maker's file-sharing partner and a logistics-firm attack starved Japan's frozen-food deliveries to thousands of clients.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Ransomware Squeezes Swiss Rail Maker and Japan's Food Supply

topics.title: Laundry Bear Runs Zero-Click Zimbra Webmail Espionage
topics.latest_developments: Researchers and CISA named the Russian group Laundry Bear, also tracked as Void Blizzard, and detailed a zero-click technique in which opening a booby-trapped message triggers JavaScript that lifts the last 90 days of mail, the full organizational email directory, browser-saved passwords, and two-factor recovery codes.
topics.summary: Russian state-supported actors have compromised Western government and commercial organizations running Zimbra Collaboration Suite since at least July 2025. Administrators should apply the Zimbra patch and reset exposed passwords and 2FA recovery codes.

sources.title: Russian Espionage Group Exploited Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Mail and 2FA Codes
International alert spotlights Russia-linked attacks on Zimbra webmail
Russian Global Webmail Espionage
Russian hackers exploit Zimbra zero-click flaw for email theft

topics.title: Ransomware Squeezes Swiss Rail Maker and Japan's Food Supply
topics.latest_developments: Swiss rail manufacturer Stadler Rail rejected a 10-million-Swiss-franc ($12.3 million) demand from the Everest gang, which stole technical data through a supplier's file-sharing platform using compromised credentials, while a ransomware attack on a Japanese food-and-logistics firm choked frozen-food deliveries to thousands of clients, including Kentucky Fried Chicken franchises.
topics.summary: Ransomware crews keep hitting manufacturing and food supply chains through third-party file-sharing and logistics systems. Firms should harden supplier credentials and segment shared platforms.

sources.title: Swiss rail manufacturer Stadler refuses to pay $12.3 million ransom after cyberattack
Swiss train maker Stadler refuses Everest $12 million ransomware demand
Ransomware Attack Puts a Chill on Japanese Frozen-Food Chain

topics.title: Malware Rides GitHub Actions and Notepad++ Plugins
topics.latest_developments: Researchers found attackers turned compromised GitHub repositories into distributed attack infrastructure, pushing malicious development versions of 10 Packagist packages tied to developer dinushchathurya between July 12 and 13, 2026 to hijack GitHub Actions runners and hit cPanel and WebHost Manager servers, while Ukraine's CERT caught LunchPoke, malware disguised as a Notepad++ plugin and bundled with the genuine editor to establish persistence.
topics.summary: Attackers keep hiding inside trusted developer and desktop software so malicious code looks like ordinary activity. Teams should pin package versions, audit CI runners, and vet third-party plugins.

sources.title: Attackers Weaponize GitHub Actions Runners to Target cPanel and WHM Servers
Hackers abuse Notepad++ plugins to stealthily install malware

topics.title: EU Fines Google $1 Billion as U.S. Curbs Scammer Visas
topics.latest_developments: The European Commission fined Google 890 million euros ($1 billion) for favoring its own services in search and the Play Store in breach of the Digital Markets Act, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio imposed U.S. visa restrictions on individuals tied to transnational cyber-scam operations.
topics.summary: Regulators pressed platform gatekeepers and cybercrime networks on the same day, one through antitrust penalties and the other through travel bans. Companies and scam operators alike face rising legal and financial exposure.

sources.title: EU fines Google $1 billion for search, app store antitrust violations
State Department imposes visa restrictions on foreign cyber scammers

topics.title: China-Nexus JadeProx Deploys TriBack Loader
topics.latest_developments: Group-IB exposed JadeProx, a China-nexus cluster it uncovered on an exposed Alibaba Cloud server in the Singapore region in mid-April 2026, deploying a previously undocumented Windows loader called TriBack Loader against government, healthcare, and education organizations across Asia and Latin America.
topics.summary: JadeProx is a newly disclosed Chinese espionage operation whose TriBack Loader delivers follow-on malware to public-sector and healthcare targets. Defenders should hunt for the loader's indicators and lock down exposed cloud servers.

sources.title: China-Nexus JadeProx Uses New TriBack Loader in Government and Healthcare Attacks

topics.title: Microsoft Passkey Flaws Revive Old Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Ahead of Black Hat USA 2026, researchers disclosed exploitable flaws in how Microsoft handles passkeys that let attackers impersonate privileged users, showing that older attack techniques still defeat the login method sold as phishing-resistant.
topics.summary: Weaknesses in Microsoft's passkey implementation undercut a control organizations increasingly trust for high-privilege accounts. Administrators should track Microsoft's fix and reinforce passkey enrollment and recovery paths.

sources.title: Flaws in Passkey Implementation Show Old Attacks Still Work

business_politics.title: Oil Tops $100 as Houthis Hit Saudi Tankers and Bonds Sell Off
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent crude settled above $100 a barrel on July 23 for the first time in two months after Iran-backed Houthis said they struck two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and Trump warned the United States weighs a "massive attack" on Iran, touching off a global bond sell-off that lifted the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level since January 2025.
business_politics.summary: The Houthi strikes threaten the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the main alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, and the resulting oil surge revived inflation fears, dragged U.S. stocks lower, and tightened financial conditions worldwide as investors reset interest-rate expectations ahead of next week's Federal Reserve meeting.

business.title: Bank of America Expands Into Greensburg
business.latest_developments: Bank of America, the second-largest U.S. bank, will open a retail branch in Greensburg, pushing its Pittsburgh-area footprint into Westmoreland County, WPXI reported July 23.
business.summary: The new location extends Bank of America's regional retail network into an adjacent county as the bank builds out its physical presence around Pittsburgh.

sources.title: Bank of America to expand Pittsburgh footprint with new Greensburg location

business.title: Walmart Eyes Mon Valley Walgreens for Delivery Depot
business.latest_developments: Walmart is weighing a shuttered Walgreens in the Mon Valley for one of its "Spark Shop" last-mile delivery depots, WPXI reported July 23.
business.summary: Walmart's Spark Shops turn former drug stores into hubs where gig workers pick up and deliver e-commerce orders to nearby customers, and the Mon Valley site would be among the first of its kind in the Pittsburgh area.

sources.title: Walmart considering closed Walgreens in the Mon Valley for last-mile depot

business.title: Deed Fraud Hits Allegheny County Homeowners
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported July 23 that some Allegheny County homeowners found county property records listing their houses as sold when they never sold them, the signature of forged-deed fraud.
business.summary: Fraudulent deeds transferred ownership of Allegheny County homes without the owners' knowledge, leaving residents to discover the theft only when official records showed their property had changed hands.

sources.title: They never sold their homes. Allegheny County property records said otherwise.

around_town.latest_developments: A large water main break shut down a stretch of Penn Avenue in Wilkinsburg on July 23, WTAE reported.
around_town.summary: The closure backed up traffic on a bridge detour that already funnels vehicles along Penn Avenue through the borough.

sources.title: Water main break shuts down Penn Avenue in Wilkinsburg, causing backups on bridge detour

around_town.title: Legionella Traces Found at Allegheny County Jail
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported July 23 that the Allegheny County Jail found possible byproducts of Legionella bacteria in employee bathrooms.
around_town.summary: Legionella bacteria can cause Legionnaires' disease, a serious form of pneumonia, making the finding in staff restrooms at the downtown lockup a health concern for jail workers.

around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported July 23 that North Strabane and Peters township police made hundreds of stops over recent weeks cracking down on aggressive driving along Waterdam Road.
around_town.summary: A North Strabane Township Police traffic study found Waterdam Road, which straddles the two Washington County townships, heavily traveled and widely speed-driven, prompting the joint enforcement push.

around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's training-camp countdown argued July 22 that Steelers defensive tackle Cam Heyward keeps defying his age, playing at an elite level and strengthening a Hall-of-Fame case as camp nears.
around_teams.summary: Heyward, the veteran anchor of Pittsburgh's defensive line and host of the "Not Just Football" podcast, has stayed among the league's best interior linemen deep into his career.

around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Off The Bat wrote July 20 that an offhand "future Yankee" comment during the Pirates-Yankees series reopened the long-running conversation about ace Paul Skenes' future in Pittsburgh.
around_teams.summary: Skenes, the Pirates' All-Star ace, stays under club control for several seasons, yet every brush with a big-market team revives speculation about whether small-market Pittsburgh can keep its best pitcher.
